q: How do I give a thumbs up to an Assistant answer?
a: Under any Assistant answer (in the Assistant panel or the Ask the coach box), click 👍. A box What should it have said? (optional) appears for a note if you want one. The rating and note stay with the answer on your computer (`coach.feedback`); nothing is sent anywhere.

q: What does Help improve the Assistant… do?
a: It opens a dialog to share the answer as an example or save it. The preview shows exactly the text that would be shared or saved (`coach.shareExample`): the question, the answer, the guide sections it used, your rating and note, the Revolution version and the page, with private names replaced by stand-ins like <clip> and <path>. You can then share it on GitHub (public, after ticking I agree), save it to a file, or close the dialog and do neither.

q: Which extras can I add to a shared example?
a: Three tick boxes, all off at the start: Include the grade's settings, Include the measured picture facts, and Include a small frame from my footage (saved as an image). The preview updates as you tick, so you see exactly what goes in. Tick them only if they help explain the question.

q: Where does Open on GitHub take me?
a: Your browser opens a pre-filled New issue page on the fork's GitHub with the label assistant-example. Check it there and submit it with your own account; nothing leaves your computer until you do. Open on GitHub needs I agree ticked first, because the example will be public and used to train Revolution's Assistant, including models released openly.

q: What does the share preview hide to protect my privacy?
a: Project, bin, clip and file names, your user and computer names, folder paths, network addresses and e-mail addresses are replaced by stand-ins such as <clip> and <path>. The preview is exactly what is shared or saved, nothing more.

q: How do I rate an answer from a script?
a: Run `coach.feedback` with the answer's `id` (from `coach.assist`), `rating` (up, down or none) and an optional `correction` (what it should have said). It stays on this computer.

q: Can a script open the GitHub page without consent?
a: No: `coach.shareExample` with route github needs `consent: true` and then returns the `url` of the pre-filled issue page. route preview returns the text, route file with a folder saves it; neither needs consent.

q: If I close the share dialog, has anything been sent?
a: No. Nothing has left your computer unless you submitted the GitHub page yourself with your own account. A 👍 / 👎 and note stay with the answer on your computer.

q: What file does Save example… write?
a: assistant-example-<id>.md in the folder you pick, plus the frame as a .png beside it if you ticked Include a small frame (the text names it). A second save never overwrites the first. Saving needs no agreement.

q: And if I'd rather not put it on GitHub?
a: Click Save example… and pick a folder: it writes assistant-example-<id>.md (and the frame as a .png if you included one), and no agreement is needed. You can keep it, check it, or send it another way. Or do neither: your 👍 / 👎 stays on your computer and goes nowhere.
